releases.name: Noosphere 1.15.1
releases.body:
Coordinated application and integration release. Artifact publication and production
activation are independently verified through the coordinated release procedure.

### Security
- Raise the MCP direct Zod minimum to `^4.6.7` and refresh its lock for
  GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (oversized constrained-collection memory exhaustion).
  OpenCode/Kilo now select the published maintained SDK revisions
  `1.15.5-noosphere.4` / `7.3.1-noosphere.5`, which declare Zod `4.6.7`.
- Add explicit full-scope provisioning for new dedicated bootstrap ADMIN
  credentials used by guided installers. Direct Compose remains opt-in via
  `NOOSPHERE_BOOTSTRAP_FULL_ACCESS`; existing key scopes, permissions, revocation
  and principal binding are preserved rather than broadened or reset. Conflicting
  credentials fail safely. Per-tool WRITE credentials remain public-only, and
  global key management continues to require ADMIN plus literal `*` scope.
- Switch OpenCode/Kilo to maintained SDK/Effect aliases that explicitly require
  TOML 5.0.1 for GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p, GHSA-9j65-hcg3-gc64 and GHSA-9qmh-m7c6-f92p,
  with public-registry locks and checks of the exact packed adapters.
  The shared client remains bundled and unpublished. TOML tables now have null
  prototypes and unsafe integers fail; see [qualification and release limits](vendor/toml5-candidate/README.md).
- Pin root DOMPurify to 3.4.17 through an override for
  [GHSA-c6gr-qvv4-5v3f](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/security/advisories/GHSA-c6gr-qvv4-5v3f)
  (XHTML/SMIL attribute guard),
  [GHSA-mrv2-3pqr-j5jr](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/security/advisories/GHSA-mrv2-3pqr-j5jr)
  (IN_PLACE hook handling) and
  [GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/security/advisories/GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7)
  (SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES shadow-root handling). The upload sanitizer uses the default
  HTML parser and excludes SMIL animation elements; it enables neither IN_PLACE
  hooks nor SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES. These are defense-in-depth/audit updates for that
  upload path. Review the exact override when updating its requirers: overrides
  can force a version below a future transitive minimum.
- Refresh the MCP `ip-address` lock to 10.7.4 for the IPv6 zone-identifier
  regular-expression denial of service,
  [GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5](https://github.com/beaugunderson/ip-address/security/advisories/GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5).
  It arrives through `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` → `express-rate-limit` for HTTP
  transport support. Noosphere's CLI uses stdio and does not construct that HTTP
  transport; this is an audit-driven dependency repair, not a demonstrated
  reachable exploit. Audit thresholds are unchanged. Existing MCP consumer
  lockfiles may need a dependency refresh to pick up the patched transitive.
- Require ADMIN permission plus explicit full content scope (`*`) for global
  API-key list, metadata, creation, updates (including self-updates) and revocation.
  Scoped ADMIN credentials can no longer mint or upgrade wildcard credentials to
  bypass content-scope boundaries. This intentionally removes key-management
  access from existing ADMIN API keys without `*`; human ADMIN sessions and
  explicitly full-scope ADMIN keys retain access. No keys are auto-expanded.

- Update Next.js and its ESLint configuration to 16.4.2 for the App Router
  Server Actions denial-of-service advisory GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r and to satisfy
  the patched Next.js floor for GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw. The existing sharp 0.35.5
  lock already implements the latter advisory's documented image workaround;
  this update does not claim a reproduced exploit or change audit thresholds.
- Refresh the root application's sharp lock to 0.35.5, including its patched
  prebuilt libvips/librsvg dependencies (GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w), and source-map-js
  to 1.2.2 (GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q). Both updates stay within existing dependency
  ranges; unrelated dependency advisories remain tracked separately.
- Add a local private `braces@3.0.3` derivative candidate

releases.name: Noosphere 1.15.0
releases.body:
# Noosphere 1.15.0

A coordinated maintenance release for the application and all integrations, carrying the OpenClaw credential-reference fix and dependency security updates.

## Fixed

- OpenClaw now discovers Noosphere's API-key secret declaration at the required top-level `configContracts.secretInputs` location. File/other host-managed SecretRefs can be resolved before plugin initialization instead of being rejected as unresolved objects. Runtime credential guards remain intact. (#345)

## Security

- Next.js and its ESLint configuration updated to **16.3.8**, including the `next/og` ImageResponse RCE fix and subsequent security fixes.
- DOMPurify updated to **3.4.16**; brace-expansion updated to **1.1.21 / 5.0.12**.
- MCP dependency updates: Hono **4.13.7**, ip-address **10.7.3**.

## Upgrade notes

- All application, npm integration, and Hermes bundle versions are coordinated at **1.15.0**.
- This release adds no database migration and does not change hybrid-retrieval defaults.
- Updating a managed OpenClaw plugin may require the host's normal metadata/permission review and activation/restart procedure. Do not replace SecretRefs with plaintext keys or bypass credential validation.
- Use the attached checksum files to verify installer and Hermes assets. Existing stateful installations still require their documented backup and upgrade procedure; publishing this release does not upgrade a running installation automatically.

See [the changelog](https://github.com/SweetSophia/noosphere/blob/v1.15.0/CHANGELOG.md) and [coordinated release contract](https://github.com/SweetSophia/noosphere/blob/v1.15.0/docs/COORDINATED-RELEASE.md).

releases.name: Noosphere 1.14.1
releases.body:
# Noosphere 1.14.1

Coordinated recovery release for the 1.14 line. The 1.14.0 application image was published, but the integration packages and GitHub Release were not completed. Use **1.14.1** for the complete set of application, installers, and integrations.

- Refresh dependency locks to resolve the `fast-uri` and `undici` security advisories that blocked npm publication. No application or integration behavior changes from 1.14.0.
- Carries the 1.14.0 wiki draft/publication controls and revisioned hybrid-retrieval evaluation tooling. Hybrid serving defaults and deployment state are unchanged.
- Publishes the AMD64/ARM64 application image, five npm packages (injected-memory helper, OpenClaw, Opencode, Kilo Code, MCP), and the Hermes provider bundle from one reviewed merge commit.

See [the changelog](https://github.com/SweetSophia/noosphere/blob/v1.14.1/CHANGELOG.md) and [recovery PR #344](https://github.com/SweetSophia/noosphere/pull/344).

The six attached files are the checksum-pinned launcher, backend installer, Hermes archive, and their SHA-256 checksum files. Publishing this release does **not** activate or upgrade an existing deployment; follow the backup and rollback procedure before any production upgrade.

Patch release so first-time installer images no longer seed house project topics, and so wiki topic delete is discoverable.

## Fixed
- Generic bootstrap topics ([#322](https://github.com/SweetSophia/noosphere/pull/322)): default Projects children no longer include PK-PRO or IHK Study Trainer. Noosphere remains. Wiki home admin entry is Manage Topics; admins can delete an empty leaf from the topic page.

## Added
- Work-VM Hermes installer hybrid runbook ([#321](https://github.com/SweetSophia/noosphere/pull/321))
- Hybrid retrieval operator activation ([#318](https://github.com/SweetSophia/noosphere/pull/318)) — llama.cpp only, not Ollama

## Security
- Kilo and Opencode lockfiles: transitive `toml` 4.1.1 → 4.3.0

Checksum-pinned launcher: commit `4468cbb160c1b5eb98d42662229287be013692d7`, sha256 `781c1f635082aefaf62910bc2d973e22809ca690ef30a1c3a7143e8c9441e283`.

Image: `ghcr.io/sweetsophia/noosphere:1.13.3` index digest `sha256:ffe13fb9a912e9227576caedfb1abf63f7fddb436a14eb6c8778c36636658ec0`.

releases.name: Noosphere 1.13.2
releases.body:
Coordinated patch release publishing the Codex MCP integration (#313) and bounded `recall_memory` fix (#314), plus the OpenClaw credential-origin binding (#312), host-owned SecretRef resolution (#301), and dependency/parser hardening (#293, #294) merged since 1.13.1.

Installer rerun preservation floor: post-run article verification is now bound to the exact pre-bootstrap live article count, so legitimate zero-article installs can be rerun immediately.

Reviewed as PR #317 from head `ee50bfec`; merged as `11e1be9b`. All post-merge workflows green on the exact merge SHA.

Upgrade via the checksum-pinned installer; see INSTALLATION.md.
